name: Kali Linux
description: A full Kali Linux desktop in your browser. KDE Plasma with Kali's security toolset, opened as a workspace window — no VNC client, no local install. Everything you change sticks: your home directory, settings and any package you apt-get survive restarts and app updates, and this workspace's repos are mounted read-only so you can open them from a real desktop.

volumes.reason: The desktop's whole home directory — KDE profile, Firefox/Burp state, ~/Desktop, and the apt/dpkg changes linuxserver's image keeps under /config. Without it every container recreation (app update, workspace redeploy) resets the machine to a fresh Kali. Ported from the monolith's ./data/aw-kali:/config bind (agentic-workspace src/config/aw.json docker_services aw-kali).

linuxserver's init hook — every executable script dropped here runs as root before the KDE session starts. This is how the monolith delivered its PipeWire/V4L2 bridge (tools/aw-kali/custom-cont-init.d/10-pipewire.sh). An app package dir is immutable and the runtime only binds $AW_APP_DATA / $AW_WORKSPACE_* sources, so pointing the hook at app data is what keeps the stock upstream image extensible without forking it into a custom build.

This workspace's checkouts, so the desktop can open/read them from Dolphin, an editor, or a shell. Read-only on purpose: the monolith mounted the whole workspace read-write (.:/home/abc/agentic-workspace:cached) and a GUI session could scribble on the live tree. Writes belong in /config.

skills.description: Use the Kali Linux browser desktop — what is mounted where, what persists, and the device/webcam limits of running it as a Tier-2 app.

timezone.title: Timezone
timezone.description: IANA timezone for the desktop session (e.g. America/Sao_Paulo). Changing it recreates the container.
